NbMoZrTi LRHEAs samples were prepared by vacuum arc melting. The purity of the Nb, Mo, Zr and Ti metal particles was 99.9 %. To protect the metal material from oxidation during the melting process, the chamber must first be vacuumed to a vacuum level of 1 × 10 4 Pa.
Due to the presence of refractory metal elements, the alloy ingots are re-melted at least eight times to ensure a homogeneous composition.

The specimens were subjected to high temperature vacuum annealing at 600 ◦C, 800 ◦C and 1000 ◦C, respectively, at a temperature rise rate of 10 ◦C/min, held for 10 h, and finally cooled with the furnace.

The microstructures of the alloys in both the as-cast and annealed states are typical of dendritic microstructures, with the grey and black regions corresponding to the dendritic region (DR) and interdendritic region (IR) respectively.
It is worth noting that the grain size decreases with increasing annealing temperature, with an average grain size of about 62.6 μ m for HT0 and 36.55 μ m for HT1000.

It is worth noting that the grain size decreases with increasing annealing temperature, with an average grain size of about 62.6 μ m for HT0 and 36.55 μ m for HT1000. This is mainly because annealing removes grain boundaries from the alloy, resulting in a decrease in the dislocation density, which is more conducive to the formation and refinement of the new grains, resulting in new grains of smaller size.

The dislocation density of NbMoZrTi LRHEAs in the as-cast and annealed states is mainly in the vicinity of grain boundaries, with only a small number of dislocations present within the grain boundaries.
As the annealing temperature increases, the residual stresses are released and the average dislocation density gradually decreases [ 45 ].
In contrast, in the 800 ◦C annealed specimens, the residual stresses were slightly increased due to the presence of defects on the specimen surface.

The annealing heat treatment did not result in any phase decomposition or phase transformation, further illustrating the good thermal stability of NbMoZrTi LRHEAs. However, it can be seen from the hardness that as the annealing temperature increases, the hardness of NbMoZrTi LRHEAs increases and then decreases, reaching a maximum value of 591.18 HV for HT600, while the hardness of the alloy decreases as the annealing temperature increases.
